An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns at higher energy levels. Above 8 EEV, a possible indication of a reduced cosmic ray rate emerges, although further evidence is needed to confirm a complete shutdown. Concurrently, we detect a shift in the characteristics of extremely energetic cosmic rays above 40 EEV. Specifically, the maximum penetration depth in the detector increases by nearly a meter, suggesting a change in the nature of these particles or their interaction with magnetic fields.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with an integrated luminosity of 2nb^{-1} and 2.48 TeV center-of-mass energy. This enabled the study of the modification of particle production in proton-lead collisions, specifically by comparing it to pp reference measurements at 5.02 TeV. Our analysis covers the particle modification factor $A_{\text{pp}}$ across a wide transverse momentum spectrum from 0.2 to 100 GeV/c for charged particles. Systematic uncertainties are thoroughly evaluated and incorporated into our final results.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, where basic observables follow specific commutation rules that define a free algebra at a given deformation parameter $\theta$. This paper focuses on a self-adjoint differential operator, denoted as Laplace, which serves to investigate the spectrum of noncommutative space as $\theta$ varies. Initially, an exact expression for the spectrum is provided for the zero deformation parameter, $\theta=0$, and it is then demonstrated that for a positive deformation parameter, $\theta>0$, the spectrum exhibits an infinite number of isolated critical values. This paper also identifies these critical values in three-dimensional space and presents explicit expressions for the associated eigenfunctions, as well as the limiting behaviors of both the spectrum and eigenfunctions near these critical values.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 40 Gb/s using two channels, which is significant for global data centers and submarine cables. However, transmitting such signals over long distances using optical cables is challenging due to chromatic dispersion. Our experiment successfully overcame this obstacle by applying optical phase compensation prior to conversion to the electrical domain, utilizing two electro-optic modulators in a differential arrangement. Successfully achieving this compensation, we used low-speed electrical signal measurements with a max frequency of 15 GHz in initial experiments, subsequently developing methods for chromatic dispersion compensation in four-channel systems and utilizing adaptive equalization to converge on a 15 GHz convergence solution.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal TCN variants from a single starting model, surpassing the performance of custom-designed networks in both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for all LHC energy levels in heavy-ion collisions. Although previous analyses have focused on comparing fluctuation properties across different energy levels, this study takes a novel approach by examining the fluctuations of particle flow patterns themselves in each individual collision. By combining this approach with a new parameter, $\sigma_\eta v_n$, which quantifies the spread of a specific angle, this study finds that the fluctuations increase with LHC energy levels and are better predicted by combining two types of flow, known as radial and anisotropic flow, for lower energy levels. However, this predictive relationship becomes less accurate at the highest energy level.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our proposed method effectively employs ALBA's rules and algebraic language to reverse its computations in the DLE setting, thereby allowing the derivation of an inductive formula from its first-order correspondent.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Many existing methods for managing incomplete data assume the absence of such violations, which is often unrealistic. In contrast to prior work, we do not restrict our approach to specific types of inconsistencies. Instead, we examine a wide range of common data quality problems, including key violations, relational conflicts, and conflicts with hierarchical rules. Our proposed solution involves generating a set of possible interpretations, each representing a coherent data view. Furthermore, we determine the most plausible interpretation based on a specific quality measure. Our methodology supports the integration of widely used schemas, such as EF schemas and MQ schemas. Notably, our approach differs from previous methods by not employing a priority-based mechanism to resolve conflicts between interpretations. Instead, we utilize a coherent possible worlds framework to identify the most plausible interpretation directly. We demonstrate our approach through theoretical analysis and experimental evaluations, even considering scenarios where tables are already complete.

This study introduces a dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson Regression, capable of capturing and forecasting the fluctuations in count-like phenomena that change over time. We demonstrate the TVPR's effectiveness using real-world data on COVID-19 daily new cases in the state of Rio de Janeiro, revealing a distinct seasonal pattern that standard Poisson regression models fail to account for.

Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs) create a bridge between object geometry and function, enabling a narrow learning approach that can be applied to a wide variety of objects within a category. This method excels at handling complex and unstructured items and enables a handle to represent multiple parts of an object simultaneously. Building on previous work, we refined our earlier binary NDF formulation - Neural Objects Descriptor Field for Object Locating and Manipulating (NODOM) to a continuous form, which refines object interaction and performance. Furthermore, we expanded NODOM's application to objects with unknown shapes and positions by integrating a neural optimizer, which successfully retrieved an NDF network from a broader range of queries. Notably, we demonstrated enhanced performance across multiple datasets, including a new one called NWU, which features nine distinct object types without any texture. A key characteristic of our objects is their inherent rotational stability, which plays a crucial role in ensuring their equivariant behavior under rotation along the z-axis. Notably, this equivariance is broken when rotating around other axes, presenting a unique challenge for NDF-based objects.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We have performed the first in-depth analysis of the globular cluster Tononzintla 2, combining a comprehensive spectral sample of 11 members with two smaller sub-samples from other clusters (Tononzintla 20 and 2002-dwarfs-10). Using the MyStar database and a custom optimization algorithm, we obtained high-quality parameters for 13 spectra and chemical compositions for 12 of them. Our results show that Tononzintla 2's member stars share consistent chemical properties, despite the sample's wide range in temperature, metallicity, and spin. However, we discovered that the clusters 20 and 2002-dwarfs-10 may not be consistent with being field stars due to their unusual chemical properties. Furthermore, Tononzintla 2's stars exhibit unusual nitrogen enrichment and a notable sodium abundance pattern that's never been observed in any other globular cluster, indicating a unique stellar evolution path for this cluster.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined $|z_c|/R_\chi^{1/\gamma}$ to be approximately 1.607, 1.589 for $N=2, 4$ respectively. Alternatively, we have previously found $|z_c|$ to be around 2.03, 1.68 for $N=2, 4$ although these earlier results have a larger systematic uncertainty.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of functions defined as compositions of high-dimensional integrals and polynomial functions. Building on this, we (a) determined the local convexity radius of a loss function used in supervised learning with Gaussian noise, which can be represented as a conditional expectation, and (b) demonstrated the convergence of stochastic gradient descent to a set of local minima with finite excess risk for Novikov's risk function in statistical learning, which involves a combination of $L_1$ and $L_2$ norms of a function represented as a high-dimensional integral and its arguments.

Modern metasurfaces are highly functional interfaces between space and matter,  
offering seamless control over the interaction of light with physical objects,  
with this interaction occurring at intensities comparable to bulk materials,  
effectively concentrating substantial power within a minimal volume,  
and this concept is becoming essential in advanced applications such as particle  
accelerators, laser fusion, and microelectronics. Despite numerous significant  
advancements, our understanding of how dynamic metasurfaces interact with ultrafast  
optical pulses at these extreme scales remains limited, mainly due to challenges in  
measuring and controlling the necessary electromagnetic fields. This article offers a  
comprehensive review of emerging concepts in this field, including new models for  
describing the dynamics of metasurfaces, methods for controlling them with electrical  
signals, and innovative approaches for measuring and controlling light field dynamics  
using optical techniques, while also highlighting current limitations and upcoming  
directions for research.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using intervening magnesium absorption lines, detected at a high resolution with the Wesenheit function to correct for varying effects on equivalent width measurements. By combining observational astrometry with theoretical simulations, researchers found strong evidence suggesting that the Giant Arc could be a foreground structure, forming part of a massive, web-like pattern of similar features in the universe. This finding reinforces the idea that such structures are consistent with our current understanding of cosmology and large-scale formation.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration. This method leverages the atmosphere as an extended source, making it necessary to consider its surface brightness and color compared to the surrounding sky. Although the technique appears straightforward, its precision is influenced by various factors, seemingly unrelated to each other, and studies have been conducted to identify the most critical elements. A crucial discovery revealed that the position of the airmask on the detector has a far greater impact on the measurement precision than previously thought, and ways to minimize its effect have been identified. Moreover, comparisons with independent measurements confirmed that the method can provide estimates of the aerosol depth, with overestimated or underestimated results reflecting the varying total amounts of scatterers in the atmosphere.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as 3D point clouds or 2D projections to ultimately determine the 6D object pose. This survey examines the efficacy of these approaches and explores various techniques, including auto-encoders, optimization, homography, projective matrices, and homographies. We evaluate three distinct models that utilize these intermediate cues: an algorithmic processing system, a regression-based process, and a detection-pipeline process. Notably, we discuss cutting-edge advancements such as employing implicit functions via neuro-SVD to re-create 3D objects and employing convolutional hollow-sparse networks (CHSN) to model 3D point clouds. We delve into the evaluation of these methods and provide a benchmark comparison of performance.

Peridynamic theories have been developed to address issues in continuum mechanics and solid mechanics by defining new relationships in integral mechanics. 
These modifications effectively incorporate constraints for material points and their neighbors, which have been identified as inactive based on the type of material failure. 
Bond-based Peridynamics have been employed in a series of simulations to analyze the effects of shock waves on aluminum plates, even when subjected to explosive forces. 
This study makes use of peridynamic dynamics to model the aluminum plates subjected to detonation forces from TNT with varying masses, which were used to examine the plates' microstructural structure and high-speed imaging. 
Peridynamic predictions were also found to be in close agreement with experimental results and the data provided by the material's properties. 
Furthermore, bond-based Peridynamics offer a distinct benefit over conventional methods in that they can accurately model the discontinuous separation of material during the propagation of shock waves.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been effectively used in biomolecules modeling. A common advantage cited in the literature is their ability to accurately compute configurational averages over extended time periods. Unfortunately, these same methods struggle to capture short-time dynamics and coordinate correlations. We investigate the impact of various discretization schemes on the preservation of a molecule's physical properties and extended configurational averages. Our study highlights the benefits of using weak approximations and identifies efficient alternatives for simulating short-time dynamics and coordinate correlations. Furthermore, we demonstrate how strong approximation methods can be modified to achieve rapid convergence to the stationary Boltzmann distribution while maintaining correct physical behavior and long-time correlations. These improvements are illustrated through simulations of biomolecules and macro-molecules, showing enhanced performance in computing short and extended dynamical quantities and enhanced efficiency in calculating equilibrium-related values.

Numerical relativity simulations of black hole mergers with significant mass ratios yield inaccurate results. This ratio is often underestimated in gravitational wave data analysis. To address this shortcoming, we adapted a physics-based model of binary mergers to account for dark matter with wave-like properties. By applying this model to cases where both black holes are surrounded by dark matter, we derived a ratio of about 7.5, which aligns well with previous results. Alternatively, we found a ratio of roughly 3 when both black holes are of equal mass. These findings are much higher than a ratio of 1.3-1.8 reported in a recent study. Moreover, we discovered that the dark matter around the binary merger significantly influences its behavior. Specifically, we found that the binary's orbits are not circular due to the presence of an outer potential. Additionally, we found that there are two distinct phases of mass plunging into the black holes - first, the inner mass that is trapped in the orbits and then, a larger amount of mass beyond. This second phase causes a delay of about 0.05 seconds. These findings may offer a new observational signature to differentiate between mergers of equal mass black holes and those with significant mass ratios.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by both elasticity and friction. A detailed analysis in a Hilbert space reveals how the spectrum's asymptotic distribution and structure evolve. It demonstrates that specific eigenvector characteristics form a complete and orthonormal basis. Consequently, we derive the exponential stability of the associated semigroup directly. Notably, we show that under these connectivity conditions, stability is guaranteed even in the absence of elasticity along the edges.

Researchers are using acoustic lenses to manipulate sound waves for better delivery of ultrasonic energy. To create these lenses, raw materials such as acrylic (PMMA) are used, although this can lead to more scattering and absorption of sound. As an alternative, acrylate resins like Stycast 1090SI have been examined due to their advantageous properties. The study found that a Stycast 1090SI lens effectively concentrated ultrasonic energy delivered from a planar transducer, similar to a traditional PMMA lens. Not only does Stycast 1090SI exhibit better resistance to degradation, but it also exhibits better adhesion properties compared to PMMA. These discoveries suggest that acrylate resins can be a more beneficial material for acoustic lenses in the future.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. This approach is currently utilized in understanding brain connectivity in neuroscience studies. A key aspect of our framework is its creation of a separate connectivity matrix for each network layer, allowing for a more in-depth analysis of complex networks.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, without the need for preprocessing like applying a color transformation or deconvolving the camera's blur and mosaic effects. By framing the problem as a convolutional neural network with multiple convolutional layers, we propose a single network called Demosaicking-Deblurring Network (DDEN) that can convert a raw blurry image into a color, sharp one. Interestingly, this network essentially performs the deblurring and demosaicking tasks, and applies a form of convolutional deconvolution to reverse the encoding process of the raw image. To tackle image noise and prevent overfitting, we incorporate a random noise layer and a scaling learning factor. Notably, DDEN achieves this multi-step image processing in a single forward pass. We utilize the ubiquitous ImageNet for training and show competitive performance with existing methods on deblurring and demosaicking tasks in both synthetic and real-world scenarios.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal where the sphere makes contact with the water's surface. A new formula is proposed to define the boundary between surface seal and vacuum detachment based on the relationship $U/c_s = f(V/U)$, with $U$ and $V$ as the sphere's diameter and volume, and $c_s$ being the speed of sound in water. The surface seal regime follows an impulsive motion pattern, following the $UC_s \sim \rho V U_s^2$ rule, with $U_s$ being the sound wave's velocity. Charact.  The surface seal regime can be described by $C \rho U_s^2 U^2 \sim \pi R^2 P_0$, with $R$ being the sphere's radius and $P_0$ the water's initial pressure. The findings from both numerical simulations and physical experiments support this proposed formula.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover how non-unique diffeomorphism and gauge invariance terms emerge as θ-terms with generalised thresholds. This discovery signifies that both the bulk and boundary universes of the string theory possess universial symmetries.

Mobile devices are increasingly used for sensitive transactions which necessitates robust security measures through multi-domain hardware architectures. A key aspect of this architecture involves secure domain hardware running critical software, accessible only via an interface from user domain hardware. This setup requires the secure hardware to process user input and present output on their displays. We have developed a tool that automates the creation of model code for this interaction, allowing designers to specify requirements in a user-domain-oriented language. Our approach maps these needs to hardware components and interconnections, validated by checkers that ensure secure hardware compliance. As an alternative to traditional methods, our technique leverages a novel concept of requirements equivalence to validate that the generated code meets the original design intentions, providing a crucial safety measure in case of a hardware breach.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$ fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a key finding that no reinforcement learning algorithm can discover an optimal policy better than $O(\epsilon)$ under these circumstances. In contrast, we found that the Natural Policy Gradient method can be robust and is capable of learning an $\Omega(1 - \epsilon)$-optimal policy, or $\Omega(\min\{\frac{1}{\sqrt{\epsilon}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{d}}\})$-optimal in linear settings. These findings were further supported by negative results demonstrating that natural gradient descent is ineffective when corrupted by an $\Omega(\epsilon)$-fraction of data. Moreover, we found that standard policy gradient is unable to learn an $\tilde{\Omega}(1 - \epsilon)$-optimal policy in linear settings. Finally, we developed a novel, simple policy $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon})$-optimal algorithm.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development for both fundamental understanding and applications in metrology and communication systems. Quantum acoustic resonators serve as the ideal testbed for multi-phonon investigations. In this study, we observe a phenomenon in semiconductor quantum dots where multiple quantum声子 excitations lead to the emission of dark excitons. These dark excitons possess higher energy than bright excitons and exhibit reduced coupling to light, resulting in a precise and robust reference that can be accessed via optical means and triggered by acoustic resonators. The characteristics of these multiphon states, including their emission lines, are found to vary linearly with the acoustic resonator's frequency. Notably, the emission lines correspond to different multiphon states, enabling us to explore both the acousto-optical interaction and the properties of these dark states. By comparing our measurements with simulations, we have a clear understanding of the geometry of these multiphon states, and we see that the emission lines of the multiphon states can be distinguished from each other. This achievement provides a clear path for exploring quantum声子 systems in both classical and quantum regimes.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model exhibits horizontal and vertical Dirac cones at the X and $\Gamma$ points in the Brillouin zone respectively. By extending the model to include longer-range hopping terms, we're able to shift the Dirac cones off the high-symmetry points in the Brillouin zone. Experiments with cold atoms can bring the lattice structure into realization and allow for the observation of this unique band topology.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess rich SPCCSs possess strong quantum features suitable for a wide range of quantum-info-processing applications.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 monomers. Furthermore, the approach has been used to devise high-performance rubber alternatives.

A key challenge in control theory and related fields is resolving complex continuous optimization issues that cannot be addressed with simple solutions. Despite their practical applications, developing efficient numerical algorithms for these optimization problems has proven difficult. This research proposes a new method using backpropagation through time to create a fast and reliable solver for optimization problems involving differential equations. This approach allows for the application of established discrete solver techniques, such as multiple-shooting methods, to these optimization issues. The results of this study show that the proposed method converges to a locally optimal solution as long as the underlying learning problem has a locally optimal solution. The paper also highlights several advantages of this approach, including its ability to leverage existing, well-developed tools and frameworks, and its potential to be implemented on GPUs for real-time optimization problems. The study provides code and data available openly online and demonstrates the method's efficiency on various optimization problems, highlighting its potential for broader applications.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be challenging for radiologists due to the need for a precise, manual outline over the entire extent of the tumor. This process is time-consuming and often inconsistent for initial size estimation. Various approaches have been implemented to aid radiologists in these complex cases, including the use of multi-phase CNNs that generate then correct tumor outlines, but these methods require complex post-processing to produce the necessary extra images. A simpler solution is presented where the CNN directly generates the tumor outline from the original scans using specialized positions in the input that guide the drawing process, potentially reducing or eliminating the need for additional images. This method demonstrates comparable performance to existing approaches and is particularly effective in complex cases, producing clear and accurate tumor outlines. The proposed model can also generate the required additional images directly from the original scans, facilitating radiologists in their complex cases.

The expense of drilling offshore wells is substantial, often exceeding $10 million per well.  During the drilling process, which can take several weeks up to a couple of months and involve multiple drill bits, accurate well placement in the planned reservoir is essential due to the high financial cost of well placement errors. To guide the drilling process towards achieving this accuracy, geosteering is employed, involving real-time analysis of geological data to adjust the well's trajectory. Traditionally, well placement is assessed using production data post-drilling completion, but this approach comes too late to avoid potential issues with well positioning. Moreover, it is hypothesized that incorrectly placed wells can lead to reduced production rates and unexpected pressure drops. We present a method based on causal discovery from scalar and vector flow data obtained during the well testing and production phases. This data can guide well placement decisions during geosteering. Our proposed approach uses a combination of treatment variables, including coil tools used during the well testing process, and a causal discovery model to analyze their effects on pressure drops and production rates. We demonstrate how these effects can aid in forming a reservoir model and making well placement decisions during geosteering. As a case study, we apply our approach to a field data set from a marine well in the North Sea, placing it in a sand unit during geosteering. Post-completion well testing and production data are used to validate our approach. Our findings suggest that the pressure drops are driven by changes in the perforated pressure zones

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing (NLP) that serves as a building block for numerous NER applications. One of the most challenging aspects of NER is the nested named entities (NEs), where certain NEs are contained within others. In this paper, we introduce a novel network-based holistic NER framework that effectively models nested NEs by reconstructing the semantic connections between them. Unlike traditional linearly sequential NER methods, our holistic approach breaks down the NER task into two components: identifying potential NE starts and predicting NE types, both of which are modeled using bi-directional long-short term memory networks with attention mechanisms. To enhance performance, we employ an adaptive gate structure and a multi-granularity attention mechanism. Our framework was tested on three publicly available datasets, and our proposed method achieved superior performance compared to other network-based methods. Moreover, our model was easily integrated into natural language understanding (NLU) tasks, and its success in improving the performance of an NLU task was notable. Our framework's source code is available on GitHub at https://github.com/huashan20/HoB-NER.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference. We look at curves defined by equations that are smooth, or at least have smooth properties in certain situations, over such modified fields. We express obstacles to counting these curves and their associated tangencies by altering the structure of these curves and their starting properties, focusing on edges and how they are affected. We show that by understanding how these curves and their starting properties change when modified, we can calculate the relative importance of these curves when counting them using these specific algebraic structures, or "GW-multiplicity". This allows us to verify a previously proposed mathematical relationship involving these curves and their counts. This verification relies on a deeper understanding of how the algebraic structures of these fields are related, especially when these fields are modified to have special values.

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal, interference-free results, we have achieved a level of accuracy of less than half a metre using actual hardware.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds have broad optical properties, making the specific properties of Ta2O5 remain unknown. To gain insight, a combined theoretical approach was used to analyze bulk and nanoscale Ta2O5. Results from this study and experimental data show that Ta2O5 has a moderate level of conductivity and is suitable for nonlinear optics, displaying very low loss in a narrow frequency range, which has the potential for use in hadron therapy for cancer treatment. Additionally Ta2O5 is compatible with silicon and possesses intrinsic chemical stability. Furthermore Ta2O5 demonstrates linear and significant nonlinear refraction coefficients along the crystallographic direction. In addition Ta2O5 has a higher effective mass and effective conductivity compared to silicon. Finally Ta2O5 has a lower effective mass and effective conductivity than other low dielectric materials. In addition the study found that the Ta2O5 crystal can be doped with Si and O, which can adjust its electronic properties. In addition the Ta2O5 compound can be doped with Si and O, which can adjust its electronic properties. In addition the Ta2O5 compound can be doped with Si and O, which can adjust its electronic properties.

Previous studies have linked microlevel traits to macrolevel phenomena but often overlook how macrolevel phenomena influence individual experiences and behavior. We aim to address this gap by showing how a macrolevel factor, state level division of labor, affects individual users' media usage and information dissemination on Twitter. Analysis of over 45 million Twitter users and 20 million accounts across 50 US states revealed that individuals in states with a high division of labor are more likely to share news and are less likely to share fake news. This influence is mediated by topdown allocation of financial resources to local media but not localist individualism. Our findings highlight the need for further integration of theory and methodology in complex systems to prevent circular reasoning and better reflect the interconnected nature of social systems.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called HALFADO. HALFADO utilizes a limited number of human judgments to effectively identify anomalies in real-time, high-frequency data streams. Implementing a sophisticated, user-friendly interface using deep learning techniques, we demonstrate the success of HALFADO in providing real-time warnings of major historical terrorist attacks as they unfold.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of a teacher's extensive shared knowledge and innate ability to convey concepts through speech. Although several approaches have been developed to charactize audio from humans giving verbal instructions without spoken words, many do not account for non speech sounds such as movement noises, nor do they exploit visual input, which is crucial for interpreting audio signals and linking them to seen events. To address these limitations, our research aims to characterize audio from humans giving verbal instructions, taking into account non speech sounds and with the benefit of visual input. In our study, we demonstrated our methods by teaching a robot how to grasp objects, using audio signals combined with visual input. We charactized four distinct types of features - speech sounds, object movement noises, voice  vibrations, and emotional expressions. Our results demonstrate that audio signals - speech sounds, object movement noises, voice  vibrations, and emotional expressions can be effectively segmented. Furthermore, we found that all these features play a significant role in helping the robot learn the tasks being demonstrated.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define and measure due to its infinite Hilbert dimension. However, conformal field theories in 2+1 dimensions offer a more manageable scenario. Using the canonical 'Fidelity Approximate Complexity' (CAC) measure, we calculate the time-dependent CAC for semi-classical CFT states, specifically those described by small graviton perturbations on Anti-de Sitter space. These calculations are made with respect to a specific family of operators, and we choose the past and future states to be created via a quench process from an NLM state, which also corresponds to forming a small star in Anti-de Sitter space. Our results for time-evolving CAC match the volume of the slice through the star's geometry, as predicted by the holographic complexity equals volume (HCVT) proposal, and we also establish the link between the rate of complexity growth and the bound Sd.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper introduces AutoConversationalTestFramework, a novel automated testing framework for conversational systems that allows for the automatic generation and modification of test cases to evaluate the performance of such systems.

For example, based on existing measurements of planets up to about Neptune, such a discovery would be fairly uncertain; however, extending the range to include Mars through Neptune plus "Planet X" would yield a more definite result with a definite uncertainty level of approximately five percent at roughly twenty AU. Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers two significant advantages: firstly, it enables vast amounts of monolingual data to be incorporated into TM; secondly, both the memory retriever and the NMT model can be jointly optimized for translation objectives. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves substantial gains in performance and outperforms TM-augmented NMT baselines even when utilizing bilingual TM. Furthermore, our model's capacity to tap into monolingual data allows it to excel in low-resource and domain adaptation scenarios.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data using a machine learning tool called HawkingNet, and initially found potential anomalies resembling low-variance circles and Hawking points. However, these anomalies were later removed, and upon re-examination, low-variance circles were found to exist regardless of their location on the sky. These findings are consistent with the expectations of CCC theory. Additionally, we found no difference in the distribution of temperatures in the vicinity of these circles, as had been previously claimed.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in preferable models. The framework's ability is further showcased by the substantial improvement it yields over baseline models and the comparable performance it achieves to existing methods on datasets like miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and cross-domain benchmarks (miniImageNet to CUB-200-2011).

Cross-domain recommendation has gained significant attention in recent years due to the widespread scarcity of item labels in many industries. Traditional CDR approaches that rely on separating domains are limited by the need to train models independently on each isolated domain. To address this problem, a new model called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) was proposed, which leverages multiple sparse domains for enhanced accuracy. The key innovation of MSDCR is its use of a factorized multi-domain layer to learn implicit high-dimensional features for items and users across different domains by collaboratively training a sparse domain layer for each specific domain. Furthermore, a multi-task learning mechanism was employed to facilitate collaboration between domains and facilitate the transfer of implicit features from one domain to another. This was achieved by balancing the tasks of predicting ratings in each domain during collaborative training. Our comprehensive evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate the efficacy of MSDCR, resulting in superior performance compared to state-of-the-art single-domain and cross-domain recommendation models.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context are any defined subsets in Euclidean space with a finite-dimensional structure and properties defining a convex cone. We have developed a comprehensive framework for managing and solving these diverse cones on a local computing environment. This system enables users to input any defined exotic cone, obtain its mathematical description, derivative, and epigraphical function, and efficiently solve a wide range of benchmark problems using multiple internal optimization solvers. Furthermore, this platform is versatile enough to support N-dimensional structures and has already seen successful emulation of well-known cones such as second-order, semidefinite, and entropy cones. ExoticCones can also facilitate the development of new solvers by providing developers with access to a wide variety of diverse cones for testing purposes. ExoticCones is freely available for use on Python 3 environments at https://github.com/raffaello-rizzoli/ExoticCones.

The ultimate goal of automated quality control in medical image analysis is to detect faulty data. To achieve this, it's crucial to have an effective method for identifying anomalies. Traditionally, anomaly detection is addressed by creating two separate models: one for a predefined task and another for an anomaly classifier. This two-step process is analogous to training a person for a specific job and then providing them with additional feedback to identify mistakes. Nonetheless, there are several quality issues facing Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) that make it necessary to develop robust automated QC systems. These problems include variations in MRI machine settings, differences in how images are aligned, and variations in how they are pre-processed. Moreover, a significant challenge in creating anomaly detectors is obtaining a comprehensive and diverse set of abnormal MRI data for training purposes. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel two-stage framework called Anomaly-Aware Network (AAN) for both training and inferring magnetic resonance images. During AAN training, we introduce an extra anomaly-aware branch with an associated loss function to make the network more sensitive to anomalies. This is done by introducing an auxiliary task where the anomaly-aware module learns to classify normal and abnormal images. Notably, AAN does not require any abnormal data during training. Instead, it generates synthetic abnormal images by artificially introducing motion artifacts and alignment differences. These altered images are then used to train a binary anomaly classifier. To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) is introduced as a computer memory solution. Although it shares the same form factor, voltage, and bandwidth as DRAM, Optane DC PMM possesses additional capabilities, including non-volatility and an addressable write-through interface. These features allow for the development of file systems and applications that don't require checkpointing or recovery, while also lowering the cost of storage. Despite these clear benefits, fully taking advantage of Optane DC PMM's properties requires a more intricate programming model and can be more expensive than simply using DRAM for program data. In contrast to traditional persistent file systems that rely on byte-granular addressing and exacerbate the performance impact of Optane DC PMM's order-preserving but non-invertible rebuild process, a simple write-through interface similar to DRAM is preferred. Building on these considerations, a new persistent memory hierarchy is designed with Optane DC PMM as primary memory and includes two distinct middle layers and DRAM as the final outer layer. In response to the limitations of existing solutions, two specialized middle-layer components are proposed to allow for in-memory persistent data structures, reducing synchronization overhead and restoring deleted data, respectively. As a result, applications can be developed that utilize write-through access, ensuring data persistence at a fraction of the cost of DRAM. In performance tests, the proposed solution with two new middle layers demonstrates comparable efficiency to a DRAM baseline while delivering up to 5.7

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We analyzed their full-potential cubic Heusler structure using DFT. GdSn3 and CmSn3 both display metallic behavior, with CmSn3 also showing a paraferromagnetic property. GdSn3 is found to be ferromagnetic with a magnetic moment of 7.44 $\mu_B$. In the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, increasing Cm content reduces both total and per-Gd magnetic moments due to a decrease in both the 4f and 5f electron U values. All GdxCm1-xSn3 compounds display a full-potential cubic Heusler structure stability of 0.17 eV/atom. The magnetic properties of these samples are investigated and analyzed, with key outcomes showing potential for further exploration.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary. In this work, various approaches to compute the scattering of W bosons within the bilepton model are discussed and the associated experimental evidence is examined.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection between the length of a group element's ordered generating sequence and its Coxeter length.

Utilizing the Pantheon supernova sample and a new approach, we've developed a method to quantify the impact of dark matter on the observations of Type Ia supernovae through weak lensing. By comparing halos to the cosmic background, we calculated the lensing effect of dark matter halos on a specific sample of supernovae, obtaining an average difference in magnitude of $0.046$ magnitudes with a standard deviation of $0.064$ magnitudes. This technique can be applied to any dataset of Type Ia supernovae and does not require knowing the exact locations of these supernovae or the lensing halos. We believe this model can offer a means to constrain the properties of dark matter by analyzing large datasets of Type Ia supernovae in the future.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks requires reliable local quantum transducers in silicon that can interface between photons and electron spins. T-type radiation damage centers in silicon come naturally pre-connected to electron spins via photons, and research has shown that they exhibit excellent optical and electronic properties with outstanding potential for quantum network nodes. However, due to the variety of configurations for both the damage centers and their environments, a thorough understanding of their precise states is essential. Through a comprehensive analysis of available experimental data, we identify two damage center states that effectively describe the observed features and demonstrate significant sensitivity to structural variations. These two states exhibit notable differences in both optical and electronic properties, and our findings provide a framework for further exploring and engineering this class of damage centers in silicon.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by comparing conventional image processing methods, such as morphological analysis and regional growth algorithms, in order to explore their application and effectiveness.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs present a significant challenge for discovering exoplanets, as their stellar activity masks the signals from these celestial bodies. This problem requires an effective method for filtering out the stellar activity from the data sets. We suggest that an LSTM neural network is capable of doing this task, since it can effectively capture the dependencies present in the data due to its recurrent nature. This capability has not been thoroughly investigated so far. Our study employs three public datasets consisting of M dwarf stars and uses both autocorrelation analysis and visual inspection to evaluate the performance of the LSTM in detecting stellar activity. Our experiments demonstrate that the LSTM successfully performs this task for most of the datasets. This capability has not been previously proven. However, the situation is more complicated in some cases and requires further research to resolve.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks, ensuring high reliability and performance. Firstly, a link quality estimation approach is utilized, enabling swift computation of link quality between nodes. Secondly, a hierarchical sector-based system is established to organize and coordinate nodes within each sector to minimize interference and improve data transmission. The effectiveness of these methods was demonstrated through a protocol, called HBCP, developed and evaluated in a simulated environment utilizing TinyOS and TelosB devices. The outcome of the evaluation revealed that HBCP can achieve very high reliability levels in data collection processes, particularly in large-scale networks and network structures that mimic actual deployments, and it also exhibited resilience in the face of device failures.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context in various ways.
We organize them into three categories based on their use of context:
one that doesn't use context, another that does, and a combined category.
We evaluate the effect of using context by comparing models from the first two
categories with their counterparts from the third category.
We incorporate context using context-aware object detectors from the second
category and discuss the effect of using context for recognition.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific type of Kirchhoff type elliptic system with constants in front of the derivatives in a two-dimensional space. It utilizes finite dimensional perturbation theory to establish this multiplicity of solutions.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors drawn from discrete distributions, specifically those with log-concave properties. Our research demonstrates that key inequalities, including Bonami-Gross, Borell, Isoperimetric, and Brascamp-Lieb inequalities, hold for such random vectors. Additionally, we establish that Strong Rayleigh measures exhibit analogous properties for the second-order differentials of convex functions. However, this second-order convexity approach cannot be applied to Gaussian measures, as they possess a nullity in their first non-zero derivative. To resolve this limitation, we modified the definition of Strong Rayleigh measures to include the necessary adjustments, thereby extending the first and second-order isotropic position inequalities to these new measures.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we investigate the cause of the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in hadron production, accounting for the connection between the helicity distribution $g_1$ and the twist-3 dihadron fragmentation function. Using a spectator model, we calculate the interference term between $s$-wave and $p$-wave and estimate this asymmetry at various experiments, including COMPASS, JLab 12 GeV, and the future EIC. Our analysis suggests that the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in SIDIS can serve as a key test for the dihadron fragmentation function.

We've established recently, much like our work on Deformed Special Relativity, that Fock's coordinate transformation can be developed from a novel, deformed form of the Poisson brackets.  Utilizing this approach, we successfully obtained the associated momentum transformation, which preserves the four-dimensional relationship between momentum and space, p_{\mu} x^{\mu}.  With the deformed algebra in hand, we derive the first Casimir invariant in this paper.  Following first quantization, we utilize the Klein-Gordon equation to show that Fock's spacetime corresponds to the de Sitter universe, whose spacetime radius can be defined by the invariant length representing the de Sitter hypersurface.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our proposed method consistently delivers a more accurate and relevant ranking of recommended entities. Furthermore, this approach is easy to deploy and can be applied across various domains of Wikipedia.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties of using incompatible donors. Although these methods have been fairly successful, there is still a lack of data on how they affect long-term transplant outcomes. To address this issue, our research aims to examine the impact of desensitization treatments on post-transplant survival and graft functionality. By analyzing real-world clinical records, we build machine learning models that predict these outcomes. Our experiments show that end-stage kidney disease and graft failure models have improved significantly after incorporating donor-compatibility treatment variables, whereas our acute rejection model performed better without these variables. Notably, patients treated with desensitization techniques face nearly double the risk of graft failure compared to those transplanted with compatible donors.

Implicit copulas are the primary choice for analyzing dependencies in complex scenarios due to their ability to effectively model dependence in high-dimensional spaces. The text presents a comprehensive overview of this broad category, encompassing copulas such as elliptical, skew t, factor, time series, and regression copulas, highlighting their key characteristics and applications. The discussion explains how the auxiliary representation of implicit copulas facilitates scalability and usability in statistical modeling, addressing concerns like parameter estimation, likelihood calculation, and model parsimony. The text also covers Bayesian estimation techniques for implicit copulas and the benefits of employing these models in conjunction with time series and regression models, which are the subject of current research advancements. The advantages of using implicit copulas are further illustrated through the examination of econometric applications, including analyses of macroeconomic time series and financial asset pricing.

This paper undertakes a comprehensive mathematical examination of the word2vec model, particularly in its implementation through the negative sampling loss function. We investigate how this model effectively captures the distribution of words within a given corpus, elucidating the connection between word co-occurrence and Euclidean distances between word vectors. A key contribution of our analysis is the derivation of a negative sampling loss function applicable to any term distribution. Furthermore, our study elucidates the relationship between neural network computations and probability theory. We demonstrate how the neural network's sigmoid activation function yields an estimate of the likelihood of a word co-occurring with another word, given the activation level of a corresponding neural unit. Ultimately, our research provides a theoretical framework that unifies neural network computations with probabilistic assessments of co-occurrence within a corpus.

This article presents the SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM based IDET systems as alternatives to our previously proposed optimal wideband waveforming strategy in [1].
Fair-throughput and sum-throughput optimisation problems are defined and formulated.
By leveraging an algorithm that utilizes fixed points, we derive the optimal fair-throughput and sum-throughput values for SISO-OFDM and MISO-OFDM systems.

This research introduces a new method to model the interaction of fluids with changing phases, combining level-set and embedded boundary techniques. By leveraging the strengths of these approaches, we've developed a numerical strategy utilizing Cartesian grids to efficiently handle complex boundary transformations and related numerical issues. This method enables a high-resolution representation of the moving interface through a projection function, modified locally around the boundary to simplify numerical handling. We outline our numerical scheme and present preliminary simulation results to demonstrate its effectiveness.

Current versions of the Lambek Calculus used in computational linguistics are expanded upon using unary modalities to govern structural rules affecting sentence order and phrasing. This incorporation of controlled structural operations yields derivational ambiguities missed by the original Lambek Calculus and its simplification in pregroups. To enable the compositional interpretation of the extended calculus, a compact category has been proposed; however, these proposals neglect the modalities' control aspect, limiting them to purely syntactic markers. In response, this paper proposes a categorical framework that integrates both functional and explicit modal aspects, building a foundation for a contextual interpretation of non-associative syntax in linguistic analysis.

We investigate learning Coarse Correlated Equilibria in stochastic games, where agents are motivated to maximize their long-term rewards and communicate through public messages that influence their strategies. This investigation is crucial as understanding CCE in stochastic games is a fundamental step in explaining complex dynamics of these games. To achieve this, we propose a novel class of policies that enable efficient computation of both policy and equilibrium values, distinguishing our approach from previous methods. Notably, our method is the first to effectively estimate the value of actions in stochastic games while delivering improved sample complexity for estimating value functions. Specifically, our algorithm's estimation accuracy is computationally feasible and yields significant advancements in estimating action values. To illustrate this, we show that our algorithm's accuracy is exponentially better than that of general Markov games, and we provide a detailed analysis of the underlying mechanisms. Ultimately, our research provides a substantial breakthrough in the field of multiagent learning by combining theoretical rigor with practical applicability.

An analysis of a stochastic Susceptible to Infective to Recovered model is conducted, where the model is based on an Erdős-Rényi random graph that changes dynamically as susceptible individuals connected to infected neighbours form new connections or sever existing ones. As the model is scaled to accommodate large populations, researchers obtained mathematical proofs of key properties of the model, particularly its early stages and the phase where the epidemic spreads rapidly. They also found that under certain conditions, there are sharp thresholds where the model suddenly switches between two completely different behaviours. It has been proven that these transitions are more dramatic if the model is changed to only form new connections to uninfected individuals, where the model suddenly switches from no spread to all-population infection without an intermediate scenario.

In this study, we examine Cotton solitons within the context of almost Kenmotsu 3-$h$-manifolds. Initially, we establish the incompatibility of such solitons when the potential vector field is directly aligned with the Reeb vector field.
